title: Verification — the crown jewel
description: Two questions, and they are not the same one: is the system refusing things it should, and is the verifier still checking what it claims to? The second is the one nothing else can see.

panels.title: Is the verifier still checking? (nothing else can see this)
Comparisons actually performed, per check
panels.description: A verifier that quietly stops performing a comparison still returns `accepted`, and every outcome panel stays green. This is the only view where that shows — a line going to zero is the signal, not a line going red. Expected: quote_signature, tcb_status, mrconfigid, compose_hash, image_digest, os_measurements.

panels.title: Checks running now vs. 24h ago
panels.description: A drop is either a regression or a deliberate removal. A deliberate removal needs an ADR superseding 0009; anything else means treating every acceptance since the drop as unverified.

panels.title: Is the system refusing things it should?
Verifications by outcome
panels.description: A refusal is the system working. Do not treat it as an availability problem, and above all do not loosen a check to make it pass (ADR 0009 rule 3).

panels.title: Why verifications were refused
panels.description: `mrconfigid_unsupported` is a platform change, not an attack — the two look identical if you only compare bytes, which is why the verifier branches on the prefix and reports which branch it took.

panels.title: TCB status of accepted verifications
panels.description: Should be UpToDate and nothing else. ADR 0014 makes enforcement mandatory; anything else here means a policy was widened at a call site or the override feature was enabled.
